DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue. west Triangeo Quezon City http: i/wvav, dilg.gov.ph OFFICE OF THE UNDERSECRETARY FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT MS. DESIREE L. ORDINARIO Operations Manager HLYC Trading, 1135 Aguilar Street Sta. Cruz, City of Manila Dear Ms. Ordinario: Greetings! 04 FEB OILG OPINION NO. This pertains to your letter dated 05 December 2018 seeking this Departments clarification on the application of Section 90 of RA 7160, otherwise known as the Local Govemment Code of 1991 particularly on the prohibition of mayors and governors from engaging in the practice of profession or in any occupation, and RA 6713, otherwise known as the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees. According to you, it is your understanding that based on Section 90 of LG Code, there is a prohibition for an incumbent mayor to engage in any occupation. With that premise, you then ask whether the prohibition is applicable to an incumbent mayor, who is the owner and single proprietor of a company, to participate in the actual government bidding and be eligible for an award of the government contract? In reply thereto, please allow us to partly quote first Section 90 of RA 7160, thus; "Section 90. Practice of Profession- (a) All govemors, city and municipal mayors are prohibited from practicing their profession or engaging in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives. xxxt Even the Supreme Court elucidated the rationale of paragraph (a), Section 90 by emphasizing that the prohibition for govemors and mayors to exercise their profession or engage in any occupation other than the exercise of their functions as local chief executives is provided "because they are required to render full time sewice. They should therefore devote all their time and attention to the performance of their duties. "1 I Catu vs. Rellosa, A. C. No. 5738, February 19, 2008

Along this line, it bears to note that the Local Government Code of 1991 did not define the phrase "practice of profession" nor did it define the phrase "engage in any occupation". Hence, the general rule in construing words and phrases used in law absence of a legislative intent to the contrary, it should be given their plain, ordinary, and common meaning. Hence, in the furtherance of this discussion, we deemed it proper to revisit the meaning of the words tangent to our elucidation. Webster Dictionary defines profession as a calling requiring specialized knowledge and often long and intensive academic preparation. On the other hand, occupation has been commonly defined as an activity in which one is engaged into. Hence, apparently, there is a distinction between the two in that, to exercise profession means that one has to be academically prepared, take the government examination and pass it and is registered in a government licensing body which regulates such profession. On the other hand, when one's activity does not fall within the ambit of "exercise of profession", the same can properly fall under "engage in any occupation". Whether it be one or the other, the evil sought to be prevented by the prohibition under section 90 of the Local Government Code is the possibility that local chief executives cannot devote full time and faithful performance of their duties and functions as such because their time was eaten up by the exercise of their profession or engagement in an occupation and take the precious time away from the full exercise of their functions and duties as public servants. Be that as it is, it is not impossible that a governor or mayor may have some pecuniary interest in a certain activity like business. Such interest remains to be only an interest if he or she does not actively paÄicipate in the management and the day to day operations of the said business. If, however, he or she is actively involved in the management and day to day operation of the business, then, without doubt, it can be considered as an activity "engage in any occupation" and his or her full time devotion to the functions as local chief executive is compromised which is the very evil sought to be prevented by above-mentioned provision. Accordingly, as a general rule, we see no impropriety or violation of Section 90 for a local chief executive to be an owner of a business for as long as he or she shall not actively participate in its management and daily operations. The practice of profession, however, is absolutely prohibited. With regard to the pertinent provisions of Republic Act 6713, particularly on possible conflict of interest, the Local Government Code of 1991 is not wanting to address the issue. Thus, section 89, paragraph (a) (1) provides; "Section 89. Prohibited Business an ad Pecuniary Interest (a) It shall be unlawful for any local government official or employee, directly or indirectly, to: (I) Engage in any business transaction with the local government unit in which he is an official or employee or over which he has the power of supervision, or with any of its authorized boards, officials, agents, or attorney, whereby money is to be paid, or property or any other thing

of value is to be transferred, directly or indirectly, out of the resources of the local government unit to such person or firm; The clear import of this section is the prohibition of the local chief executive to engage in any business transaction with the local government unit in which he is the local chief executive. Hence, clearly, the incumbent mayor's business cannot participate in the public bidding for the project of his own town or city. Moreover, we are also of the view that an incumbent local official is prohibited to participate in the public bidding of his component barangays because under Section 32 of the Local Government Code of 1991 , the city or the municipality, through its city or municipal mayor, shall exercise general supervision over its component barangays. Conversely, if the mayor's business will participate in a government public bidding with other Local Government Unit other than his own, or one which he has no authority to supervise, we are of the considered view that it cannot come within the prohibition under Section 89. We hope to have enlightened you on the matter. M Very truly yours, By Authority of the Secretary EL C. SACENDONCILLO, CESO Ill Undersecretary
